claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you enquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my one child - his name is Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your child Alex.

Now, let me ask you some questions to determine eligibility:

**What is Alex's date of birth?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 8 years old - he was born in 2016.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. So Alex was born in 2016 and is currently 8 years old.

**Are you responsible for Alex (for example, are you his parent or legal guardian)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm his parent and he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you and Alex both UK residents, and do you both live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

**Are you currently working or have you worked in the UK, and if so, are your earnings above or below the Child Benefit tax charge threshold?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure what the tax charge threshold is - could you explain that to me?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course! Let me explain the Child Benefit tax charge threshold.

If you receive Child Benefit, you may have to pay a tax charge if your individual income is above a certain threshold. This is called the "High Income Child Benefit Charge."

The threshold is £50,000 per year. If your income is £50,000 or less, you won't have to pay any tax charge on the Child Benefit you receive.

If your income is above £50,000, you'll have to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through self-assessment tax, depending on how much your income exceeds that threshold.

So to clarify for your situation:

**What is your annual income (or approximate annual income if you're not sure of the exact figure)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: My income is below £50,000, so I should be fine with that then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for clarifying that. So your income is below £50,000, which means the tax charge won't be an issue for you.

**Are you currently receiving any benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training, and if so, will he continue to be until after his 16th birthday?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's only 8, so he's in primary school right now. He won't be 16 for quite a while yet!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Of course - that makes sense! Since Alex is 8 years old and in primary school, he's clearly in full-time education.

**Are you currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or would this be a new claim?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: This would be a new claim - I haven't claimed it before.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just to confirm the details I've gathered about your situation with Alex:

- Alex is 8 years old, born in 2016
- You are his parent and he lives with you in the UK
- You both live in the UK
- Your income is below £50,000
- You're not receiving Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, or Pension Credit
- Alex is in full-time education (primary school)
- This would be a new claim for Child Benefit

I believe I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me now determine the outcome based on the Child Benefit rules.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Your circumstances meet all the requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Alex is under 16, in full-time education, living with you in the UK, your income is below the tax charge threshold, and you're not receiving any conflicting benefits.

You can now proceed to make a new claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions about the application process or your eligibility, feel free to ask!
